bull.b: Exceptional payment-volume growth combined with consistently high customer retention indicates that merchants are expanding usage rather than merely remaining on the platform. This supports durable share-of-wallet gains, stronger network economics, and continued revenue growth across emerging markets.

Very low leverage gives dLocal substantial financial flexibility to fund product development, geographic expansion, and technology investment without relying heavily on debt. Strong returns on equity further indicate that the company is using its capital base efficiently and can remain resilient through operating volatility.

The raised outlook demonstrates continued management confidence in merchant demand while operating leverage is improving. Higher volume growth, a growing gross-profit base, and expected automation benefits could allow earnings and cash generation to compound even if revenue growth moderates from current levels.

bear.b: The multi-year decline in gross and net margins shows that strong revenue growth has not translated proportionally into profitability. If the lower margin profile persists, dLocal may have less earnings conversion from future volume growth and reduced capacity to absorb pricing, mix, or cost pressures.

A sustained shift toward lower-priced payment flows could reduce the revenue captured per dollar of TPV, even when transaction volumes grow rapidly. This creates a risk that merchant expansion produces weaker gross-profit growth and makes future results more dependent on favorable mix or efficiency gains.

Regional gross-profit volatility indicates that reported profitability depends partly on geographic and payment-method mix, not only transaction growth. Repeated shifts away from higher-spread markets or weaker FX economics could make margins and earnings less predictable over the next several quarters.
